    21	Dear Mr. Sheehy:
    22	From May 22 to June 8, 2023, representatives of the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety
    23	Administration (PHMSA), Office of Pipeline Safety (OPS), pursuant to Chapter 601 of 49
    24	United States Code (U.S.C.), inspected Tallgrass Energy, LP’s (Tallgrass) records and
    25	procedures for the new gas integrity rule 1 in Lakewood, Colorado.
    26	As a result of the inspection it is alleged that Tallgrass has committed a probable violation of the
    27	Pipeline Safety Regulations, Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). The item inspected
    28	and the probable violation is:
    29	1.
    30	
    31	§ 192.607 Verification of Pipeline Material Properties and Attributes: Onshore steel
    32	transmission pipelines.
    33	(a) ….
    34	(c) Verification of material properties and attributes. If an operator does not have
    35	traceable, verifiable, and complete records required by paragraph (b) of this
    36	section, the operator must develop and implement procedures for conducting
    37	nondestructive or destructive tests, examinations, and assessments in order to
    38	verify the material properties of aboveground line pipe and components, and of
    39	buried line pipe and components when excavations occur at the following
    40	
    41	1
    42	
    43	Docket No. PHMSA–2011–0023; Amdt. Nos. 191–26; 192–125 Pipeline Safety: Safety of Gas Transmission
    44	Pipelines: MAOP Reconfirmation, Expansion of Assessment Requirements, and Other Related Amendments
    45	
    46	 opportunities: Anomaly direct examinations, in situ evaluations, repairs,
    47	remediations, maintenance, and excavations that are associated with replacements
    48	or relocations of pipeline segments that are removed from service…
    49	Tallgrass did not opportunistically obtain material attributes for a line segment that was
    50	relocated and replaced as required by § 192.607 and its procedure for material
    51	verification. In 2023, a segment of the Doniphan to York line was relocated and replaced
    52	to remediate anomalies. In the area of this relocation project, Tallgrass had previously
    53	identified pipe attributes as missing in its MAOP-R database. Tallgrass’ procedure
    54	entitled “OM_210G Material Verification” referenced SOP-A19, which defined, in
    55	section 2.1.5, when opportunistic testing shall be done in accordance with § 192.607.
    56	Section 2.1.5(g) specifically called out excavations associated with replacements or
    57	relocations of pipeline segments that are removed from service as a condition for getting
    58	the attributes opportunistically. As this was a relocation, those attributes (Grade, Seam
    59	Type) should have been obtained. Thus, Tallgrass failed to meet the requirements of §
    60	192.607.
    61	Proposed Civil Penalty
    62	Under 49 U.S.C. § 60122 and 49 CFR § 190.223, you are subject to a civil penalty not to exceed
    63	$266,015 per violation per day the violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,660,135 for a
    64	related series of violations. For violation occurring on or after January 6, 2023, and before
    65	December 28, 2023, the maximum penalty may not exceed $257,664 per violation per day the
    66	violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,576,627 for a related series of violations. For violation
    67	occurring on or after March 21, 2022 and before January 6, 2023, the maximum penalty may not
    68	exceed $239,142 per violation per day the violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,391,412 for
    69	a related series of violations. For violation occurring on or after May 3, 2021 and before March
    70	21, 2022, the maximum penalty may not exceed $225,134 per violation per day the violation
    71	persists, up to a maximum of $2,251,334 for a related series of violations. For violation
    72	occurring on or after January 11, 2021 and before May 3, 2021, the maximum penalty may not
    73	exceed $222,504 per violation per day the violation persists, up to a maximum of $2,225,034 for
    74	a related series of violations. For violation occurring on or after July 31, 2019 and before January
    75	11, 2021, the maximum penalty may not exceed $218,647 per violation per day the violation
    76	persists, up to a maximum of $2,186,465 for a related series of violations. For violation
    77	occurring on or after November 27, 2018 and before July 31, 2019, the maximum penalty may
    78	not exceed $213,268 per violation per day, with a maximum penalty not to exceed $2,132,679.
    79	We have reviewed the circumstances and supporting documents involved in this case, and have
    80	decided not to propose a civil penalty assessment at this time.
    81	Proposed Compliance Order
    82	With respect to Item 1, pursuant to 49 U.S.C. § 60118, the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials
    83	Safety Administration proposes to issue a Compliance Order to Tallgrass Energy. Please refer to
    84	the Proposed Compliance Order, which is enclosed and made a part of this Notice.

    87	 Response to this Notice
    88	This Notice is issued in accordance with 49 C.F.R. § 190.207(c). Any response you may have
    89	submitted to the original Notice is no longer applicable. You must respond as set forth below.
    90	Enclosed as part of this Notice is a document entitled Response Options for Pipeline Operators
    91	in Enforcement Proceedings. Please refer to this document and note the response options. All
    92	material you submit in response to this enforcement action may be made publicly available. If
    93	you believe that any portion of your responsive material qualifies for confidential treatment
    94	under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b), along with the complete original document you must provide a second
    95	copy of the document with the portions you believe qualify for confidential treatment redacted
    96	and an explanation of why you believe the redacted information qualifies for confidential
    97	treatment under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b).
    98	Following your receipt of this Notice, you have 30 days to respond as described in the enclosed
    99	Response Options. If you do not respond within 30 days of receipt of this Notice, this constitutes
   100	a waiver of your right to contest the allegations in this Notice and authorizes the Associate
   101	Administrator for Pipeline Safety to find facts as alleged in this Notice without further notice to
   102	you and to issue a Final Order. If you are responding to this Notice, we propose that you submit
   103	your correspondence to my office within 30 days from receipt of this Notice. The Region
   104	Director may extend the period for responding upon a written request timely submitted
   105	demonstrating good cause for an extension.

   107	document you submit, please provide a copy in electronic format whenever possible.
